author: mountain state times
title: West Virginia baseball prepares for Big 12 Tournament in Arizona
text:
Steve Sabins, Head Coach at West Virginia Mountaineers Men%27s Baseball - https://wvusports.com/ The West Virginia University baseball team will compete in the 2026 Big 12 Tournament, beginning their campaign on May 21 against either TCU or Kansas State at Surprise Stadium in Surprise, Arizona.
This tournament appearance is significant as West Virginia seeks its first Big 12 Tournament championship and sixth overall tournament title. The Mountaineers finished the season with a strong record of 37-12 and placed second in the Big 12 with a conference record of 21-9.
As the No. 2 seed, West Virginia earned a double-bye into the quarterfinals of this single-elimination tournament. Their opening game is scheduled for Thursday at 7:30 p.m., and fans can watch it on ESPNU. If they advance, Friday’s semifinals will be broadcast on ESPN+, and Saturday’s final will air on ESPN2. All games featuring West Virginia will also be available via audio broadcast through the Mountaineer Sports Network, with live statistics accessible at WVUsports.com.
Kansas State secured a win over Utah to start the tournament while BYU defeated Texas Tech. Before facing either TCU or Kansas State, BYU will play Baylor in another second-round matchup.
Several Mountaineer players have received recognition for their performances this season. Redshirt junior Maxx Yehl was named Big 12 Pitcher of the Year, becoming only the third player from West Virginia to earn this honor. He was joined by pitchers Chansen Cole and Ian Korn as well as catcher Gavin Kelly on the All-Big 12 First Team. Outfielder Paul Schoenfeld made the Second Team, while Reese Bassinger, Carson Estridge, Armani Guzman, Matt Ineich, and Sean Smith received honorable mentions.
Catcher Gavin Kelly leads West Virginia with a .387 batting average along with twelve home runs and forty-seven runs batted in (RBI). Kelly is also recognized as a semifinalist for both the Golden Spikes Award and Dick Howser Trophy and has been recently named by Baseball America as the top college prospect for the upcoming MLB Draft.
The NCAA selection show is scheduled for Monday, May 25 at noon Eastern Time.
